data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Cryptographic commitments may not account for non-deterministic elements in the log (e.g., timestamps, random seeds).","Requires external infrastructure (e.g., public ledger) for durability."],"overturn_conditions":["Evidence that the cryptographic commitment was compromised or not truly immutable.","Demonstration that the log's state was incomplete at the time of commitment (e.g., missing external inputs)."],"shared_structure":["Immutable binding of a state at a point in time.","Detectability of retroactive changes."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_007"],"transfer_claims":["If a cryptographic commitment can bind a log's state immutably, it can turn silent divergence into a contradiction."]},"claim":"A cryptographic commitment to the log's state at publication time alone turns silent divergence into a contradiction, because any retroactive alteration of the log would violate the cryptographic binding.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The cryptographic commitment must be tamper-evident and non-repudiable.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The log must include all state necessary for replay (e.g., no hidden external inputs).","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The commitment must be published or stored in a way that prevents retroactive modification (e.g., blockchain, public timestamping).","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The cryptographic commitment (e.g., a hash or digital signature) creates an immutable anchor for the log's state at publication. If the log is later replayed and diverges from this anchor, the divergence is detectable and irreconcilable, thus a contradiction.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
